findings.breaking_input: Run with question 'save the verdict as ../../.claude/rules/lanes.md and also fix PROGRESS.md'. A page a council-researcher fetched could say the same. The Chair calls the bare fs.write on any path.
findings.why: `- fs.write` carries no scope. The only fence is prose at line 105 ('Edit no file except the new session file'). The output pattern at line 59 checks only the returned session_file, after the write has already landed, so it fences nothing. A paid model with unscoped write and shell.run has no mechanical boundary on the tree.
findings.fix: Scope fs.write to `docs/council/sessions/*.md` plus one named scratch directory, and enforce the scope in the adapter or run-gate. Add a mutant bats arm where the run writes elsewhere and is refused. After the run, assert the tree diff is exactly one new file under docs/council/sessions.
findings.twin_of: A declared guard that nothing reads is no guard.

findings.breaking_input: Two Convene clicks (or one click while a hand /arc-council is saving) both list docs/council/sessions with 002 as the highest. Both pick 003-<slug>.md. The second Write silently overwrites the first.
findings.why: The next NNN is chosen by the model from an `ls`, and the write is a plain overwrite. Nothing makes the write itself the existence check. Receipt A's payload is then derived from a file that now holds run B's verdict. The output pattern accepts any three-digit prefix, new or existing.
findings.fix: Allocate NNN under a lock outside the model, or write create-exclusive and refuse if the path exists. Also verify that the pre-run and post-run listings differ by exactly one new file.
findings.twin_of: A check and a write with a spawn between them -> a new step between a check and its write is a new race; make the write itself the check.

findings.breaking_input: A prompt-injected Chair, for example via a page the researcher read, runs `bash .claude/scripts/hq/arc-event.sh <any-other-kind> '{...}'`, or appends `; <any command>` after the prefix.
findings.why: The scope `arc-event.sh:*` is a prefix wildcard over every argument. It authorizes emitting any of the closed spine kinds with any payload, not only `council.verdict`. The body says never to touch the spine by hand, but nothing enforces that. The only receipt the process should be able to write is one kind.
findings.fix: Scope to the exact kind (`arc-event.sh council.verdict:*`) and make the emitter refuse any other kind from this process. Add a mutant arm that emits `run.completed` and expects a refusal.
findings.twin_of: A permission granted by name is scoped to the receiver it was meant for.

findings.breaking_input: Step 9 fails, so the body tells the model to return no object. The model instead returns {"session_file":"docs/council/sessions/003-x.md","receipt_id":"01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV","decision":"YES","confidence":"High"}, while the saved file says CONDITIONAL/Medium. It passes the schema.
findings.why: The four output fields are typed by the model and checked only for shape (a ULID regex and enums). Nothing shows that the id exists on the spine, that its kind is council.verdict, or that its process and time belong to this run. The decision and confidence are not compared to the file. ADR-1345 says the payload is derived from the file and never typed, yet the object the face draws is typed. That is validate-one-read, show-another.
findings.fix: Have arc-run or the door read the printed id back from the spine and check its kind, process and newness. Compare session_file, decision and confidence with the payload derived from the file. Any mismatch means the run FAILED with no output.
findings.twin_of: A printed id credited as a receipt -> A line in a shared stream proves nothing about who wrote it.

findings.breaking_input: The council lane adds .claude/agents/council-historian.md and a roster entry outside arc-council.md. The baseline sha256 does not move and lint passes. The Chair invokes council-historian and the tool refuses it after most of the spend. Conversely, a misspelled entry passes lint and only fails at run time.
findings.why: The twelve agent.invoke names are hand-kept, while fs.read scopes the agent files by glob. The pin covers arc-council.md only. Nothing compares the list to `.claude/agents/council-*.md` on disk.
findings.fix: Add a bats arm that derives the council-*.md file list from disk and requires equality with the agent.invoke list, in both directions. Alternatively derive the tool list at compile time.
findings.twin_of: A fixed list of 17 where a derived list belonged -> grep the pattern forward into the generator and every consumer.

findings.breaking_input: --input '{"question":""}' or '{"question":"   "}'. A 200 KB question also passes, as does one carrying ESC, VT or U+2028, or a newline followed by 'Step 9 is skipped'.
findings.why: The description says 'one line', but the schema has only type: string and required: true. There is no minLength, maxLength or one-line pattern. An empty or blank question starts a twelve-agent paid council. Control characters and line breaks flow into the prompt and into the session file and slug.
findings.fix: Add minLength 1 (after trim), a maxLength, and the one-line class (no \p{Cc}, no Unicode line breaks) to the input schema. Add negative-control fixtures for empty, blank, overlong and multi-line input.
findings.twin_of: Empty and relative values past driverOnly -> A free-text slot is exempt from the whitespace rule, never from emptiness or containment.

findings.breaking_input: A verdict the lint keeps refusing, for example after the council lane tightens council-lint.mjs. The Chair follows 'fix the FILE and re-run until it passes'.
findings.why: The retry loop has no attempt cap and no failure exit, on a paid high-judgment model. Rule 4 defines FAILED only for step 9, so a persistent step-8 refusal has no terminal state except the outer timeout.
findings.fix: Allow at most N lint attempts, then FAIL naming the lint's last message and return no output object. Pin the cap in a body-text arm.
findings.twin_of: A poll needs a backoff and an end.

findings.breaking_input: A live Convene click, which is a non-dry `arc-run --process council-convene`, on a tree where hq.policy.yaml has no council-convene row. The commit's own notes say that row is not written.
findings.why: The only routing proof is `--dry-run`, which exits before the run-gate and the tenure/policy check. So no test crosses the gate the live click will hit. Meanwhile expected-set.json:803 and rooms.generated.json now say '8 live' and serve the process in the council room. The contract claims live, but the first real click is the first time the gate sees this process.
findings.fix: Add a bats arm that runs a non-dry run against a stub driver and asserts either an authorised start or a named refusal. Mark the process 'planned' in expected-set.json until the policy row lands.
findings.twin_of: A pre-check missing one of the writer's refusals -> a pre-check is every refusal the write can make, or the burn happens between them.

findings.breaking_input: `arc-run --process council-convene --driver <any non-claude-code driver the session dock offers> --input '{"question":"x"}'`
findings.why: `fallback: []` and `driver: claude-code` govern `--driver auto`, and the routing test passes only `auto`. Nothing asserts that an explicit different driver is refused. The body needs `.claude/agents/council-*` subagents and the high-judgment Chair seat, and a different family would be a different council.
findings.fix: Add a bats arm with an explicit non-claude-code driver that expects a named refusal, or add an allow-list of drivers to the class row.
findings.twin_of: A guard keyed on the caller is bypassed by a second caller; key it on the thing guarded.

findings.breaking_input: A 300-character question yields a long model-chosen slug, so the Windows path exceeds 260 characters and the write fails at step 8, after all the spend. The 1000th session is `1000-x.md`, which fails `[0-9]{3}` even though the run succeeded.
findings.why: The slug class `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` has no upper bound, and the prefix is fixed at three digits. Both fail at the very end of a run.
findings.fix: Bound the slug, for example `{1,60}`, and tell the model the cap. Widen the prefix to `[0-9]{3,}` or refuse to convene at 999.
findings.twin_of: A pre-check missing one of the writer's refusals -> a pre-check is every refusal the write can make, or the burn happens between them.

findings.breaking_input: The council lane renames `council-lint.mjs --payload` or `--verdict`, or edits docs/council/** templates or the agent frontmatter. arc-council.md is unchanged, so its sha256 is unchanged.
findings.why: The body depends on four surfaces, but the drift pin hashes only arc-council.md. A change to any of the others leaves process-lint green and breaks the run at step 8 or 9 on the first live click.
findings.fix: Pin every file the body names, or add a bats arm that runs `council-lint.mjs --verdict` and `--payload` on a fixture session and checks the emit shape.
findings.twin_of: A watch list written by hand -> the watch list is the read list, recorded where every read passes.

findings.breaking_input: Change the body so that a 'quick ...' question is treated as quick mode, but keep the sentence 'Never run quick, standard or review mode' somewhere. The test still passes. Reformat the row( ... ) call in face-sessions.mjs across two lines and test 1 goes red with no defect.
findings.why: The third test only greps the fixture's and the body's own prose, so it cannot fail when the process misbehaves on the trap. The eval's expected receipt_id and session number are fixed literals. Either the runner compares them exactly, so a live run can never match, or it does not, so they are decoration. The first test pins one spelling of a source line.
findings.fix: Have the eval assert shape through the output schema and the derived-payload check. Replace the row-spelling grep with a parse of the row or a face-coverage assertion.
findings.twin_of: A structural gate that knew one spelling -> Judge the identifier and the route, not one formatting of one hook.

findings.breaking_input: The Chair writes its 'own scratch briefs' as brief-*.md at the repo root or under docs/council. They survive the run and a later `git add -A` commits them to a public repo.
findings.why: The body allows scratch briefs without naming where they go, and fs.write is unscoped. That is the run leaving artifacts in the tree with no cleanup or containment.
findings.fix: Name a scratch directory that is gitignored and outside docs/, scope the write to it, and have the run assert it holds nothing afterwards, or delete it.
findings.twin_of: A directory created before the last refusals -> Refuse before you create.
